Base: Unauthorized Access to M2 IoTEdge Module where database secrets are used
Model: If WebSocket connections between M1, M2, and M3 on the public-access LAN are not encrypted, an attacker with LAN access can sniff network traffic and reconstruct live video frames, OCR text, and scan results as they traverse the network. Exposure of confidential video content, order information, and potentially personal or sensitive data, leading to privacy violations and regulatory non-compliance.

Base: Application Insights is connected via Connection String which is stored in .env file on the IoTEdge device. Once user gains access to the device, .env file can be read and attacker can tamper the log data.
Model: An attacker with limited access to the IoT Edge device filesystem (e.g., via another low-privileged process) modifies configuration files or environment variables that contain Azure Storage, Cognitive Service, or Application Insights connection strings. Modules may send data to attacker-controlled Azure resources, leak confidential data, or be prevented from sending data to the legitimate services; attacker also gains ability to act with the privileges of the modified connection strings.

Base: Application Insights is connected via Connection String which is stored in .env file on the IoTEdge device. Once user gains access to the device, .env file can be read and attacker can tamper the log data.
Model: A malicious actor tampers with telemetry sent to Azure Application Insights or Azure Monitor (e.g., by altering metric values or log contents in the sending modules) to hide abnormal behavior or fabricate normal operation. Security and operational monitoring becomes untrustworthy; attacks, performance issues, or data leaks may go undetected or be misdiagnosed, increasing dwell time and damage.

Base: Azure IoT Hub connection string is stored in .env file on IoTEdge Device. Once user gains access to the device, .env file can be read and attacker cause Dos attacks on IoTHub
Model: A malicious actor obtains an IoT Edge module’s credentials or identity (e.g., via stolen deployment credentials or misconfigured IoT Hub identities) and registers a fake IoT Edge device or EdgeRuntime that appears legitimate to Azure IoT Hub. Unauthorized device can receive configuration and secrets (connection strings) and send falsified telemetry to Application Insights, undermining trust in monitoring and potentially exposing sensitive configuration data.
